Why go: real off-road riding with a local guide

Most of Koh Samui's interior is steep hill country with dirt tracks between coconut and durian plantations. On an enduro bike you reach viewpoints and trails that are off-limits to rental scooters, with a guide who knows which tracks are rideable after rain.

The routes build up in length and difficulty. The beginner ride sharpens your off-road skills on easier trails; the longer loops climb to mountain viewpoints and link up tracks across the island.

Choosing a route

The beginner ride works on technique on easier trails, the scramble adds steeper climbs, and the mountain loop links the hill tracks to high viewpoints over the north and east coasts. The around-the-island ride is the longest and covers the most varied ground. Pick a shorter route if you haven't ridden off-road for a while: Samui's red clay is grippy when dry and very slippery when wet, and arms tire quickly in the heat. Morning rides are cooler and the trails are often drier.

Who it suits

  • Experienced motorbike riders who want something more serious than a scooter ride.
  • Small groups of friends who can share the transfer cost.
  • Riders comfortable taking financial responsibility for the bike.

Who should choose something else

  • Anyone without motorbike experience: choose the ATV and buggy tour.
  • Families with children: try the jungle zipline.
  • Riders without insurance that covers off-road motorbikes.

Good to know

  • Risk: off-road riding causes injuries. Ride within your limits and follow the guide's line.
  • Licence and insurance: many travel policies only pay out if you hold a motorcycle licence and ride legally. Read our motorbike guide.
  • Heat: morning starts are cooler; drink before you ride.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time.
